blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
Demand forecasting means guessing how much customers will want, before they ask. It is never exact. But a good forecast gets you close enough to plan.

Forecasters look at three things. First, history: what happened last year. Second, trends: what is growing or shrinking. Third, events: a holiday, a promotion, or a new launch. They put these together into one number. Then they watch how wrong the number turns out to be.

A forecast is not a promise. It is the best guess, made on purpose.

items.q: What is a demand forecast?
options: A guess about how much customers will want
A list of last year's sales
items.why: "Demand forecasting means guessing how much customers will want."

items.q: What three things do forecasters look at?
items.why: "they look at history… trends… events."

items.q: What do trends show?
items.why: "trends: what is growing or shrinking."

items.q: The text says a forecast is "not a promise." This suggests that…
options: the real number can be different
items.why: Inferência: se não é uma promessa, o número real pode sair diferente do previsto.

items.q: The author would most likely DISAGREE with this idea:
options: A good forecast helps you plan
A forecast can be a perfect, exact number
items.why: Inferência: o texto diz "It is never exact", então o autor discorda de um número perfeito e exato.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Sophie ensinando um planejador júnior. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Okay, let's build next month's forecast together. Don't worry, it does not need to be perfect. We just need a good guess.

First, open last year's sales. This is our history. Same month, last year — how much did we sell? That number is our starting point. Write it down.

Now, is demand growing or shrinking? Look at the last few months. If sales are going up, the trend is up, so we will add a little. If sales are going down, we will take a little away.

Next, events. There is a promotion next month. A promotion brings more customers, so demand will go up. We are also planning a small launch. That is new, so we will guess carefully.

Put it all together and we get one number. That is our forecast. It is not a promise. Next month we will check how wrong we were, and then we will do better. Any questions?
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: What does Sophie say they need to build?
options: A good guess for next month
items.why: "it does not need to be perfect. We just need a good guess."

items.q: What is the starting point for the forecast?
options: Last year's sales for the same month
items.why: "Same month, last year… That number is our starting point."

items.q: If sales are going up, what will they do?
items.why: "If sales are going up, the trend is up, so we will add a little."

items.q: Why does Sophie say the launch needs a careful guess?
options: Because it is new and has no history
items.why: Inferência: "That is new" — sem histórico, é mais difícil prever, então adivinha com cuidado.

items.q: How would you best describe Sophie's tone with the junior planner?
items.why: Inferência: "Don't worry", passo a passo, "we will do better" — ela ensina com calma e apoio.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "Our forecast for next month is 500 units." A forecast is…
items.why: Forecast = previsão: uma estimativa do que vai acontecer.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "We use last year's ___ to see what happened before."
items.why: History = histórico: o que aconteceu no passado.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "Sales are going up every month. The ___ is clearly up."
items.why: Trend = tendência: a direção em que as vendas vão.

items.q: "The forecast is not exact." Exact means…
items.why: Exact = exato: perfeitamente certo, sem erro.

items.q: "She made the guess on purpose." On purpose means…
items.why: On purpose = de propósito: de forma planejada, não por acaso.

blocks.instruction: Expressões que aparecem em reuniões de planejamento. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "The manager has to sign off on the forecast." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar, dar o aval.

items.q: "We will roll out the promotion next week." To roll out means to…
items.why: Roll out = lançar, colocar em ação.

items.q: "The sales team pushed back on the high number." They…
options: did not like it and said so
items.why: Push back on = resistir, discordar.

items.q: "We made a plan, but we need to follow through." To follow through means to…
items.why: Follow through = ir até o fim, cumprir o combinado.

items.q: "Let's keep an eye on the numbers this month." This means to…
items.why: Keep an eye on = ficar de olho, observar com atenção.
